subsystems.name: Wing or kite
subsystems.role: the flying lifting surface that generates the power; it flies fast crosswind loops to multiply the apparent wind speed.

subsystems.name: Tether
subsystems.role: the structural link carrying hundreds of kilonewtons of tension while transmitting power or data.
parts: braided high-modulus polyethylene or aramid fibres
conductive copper cores and fibre-optic line (fly-gen)

subsystems.name: Ground station
subsystems.role: the winch and generator that convert tether motion into electricity and launch and recover the wing.

subsystems.name: Flight control and avionics
subsystems.role: flies the wing autonomously in figure-eight patterns at tens of metres per second, seconds ahead of disturbances.
parts: tether load cells and winch encoders

subsystems.name: Power conversion and grid interface
subsystems.role: turns highly variable, pulsing output into compliant grid power.

subsystems.name: Safety and airspace system
subsystems.role: keeps the wing inside its approved volume and brings it down safely if anything fails.

buildSteps.title: Measure the wind aloft
buildSteps.detail: LiDAR or tethered-balloon soundings profile wind speed and direction from 200 to 600 m, confirming a steady resource and checking aviation, radar and wildlife constraints.

buildSteps.title: Design and build the wing
buildSteps.detail: Spars and skin are laid up in carbon fibre, kept deliberately light; aeroelastic simulation is essential because a wing stiff enough to be simple would be too heavy to fly well.

buildSteps.title: Make the tether
buildSteps.detail: High-modulus polyethylene or aramid yarns are braided into a rope rated well above peak tension; fly-gen versions also weave in copper conductors and a data fibre.

buildSteps.title: Fabricate the ground station
buildSteps.detail: A winch drum, gearbox and permanent-magnet machine are assembled in a container on a concrete foundation sized for peak tether pull and for the wing's landing loads.

buildSteps.title: Write the autopilot
buildSteps.detail: A model-based controller is tuned in simulation and hardware-in-the-loop rigs to fly the crosswind pattern and handle gusts, line slack and emergency recovery.

buildSteps.title: Test incrementally
buildSteps.detail: Static tether pulls first, then short flights within a small box, then full figure-eight power cycles at rising wind speeds, with each phase logged against predicted loads.

buildSteps.title: Commission the grid connection
buildSteps.detail: Inverters and protection are set up to smooth the pulsing reel-out/reel-in output, and the system is run for months to expose wear in tether, drum and bearings.

buildSteps.title: Certify and integrate airspace
buildSteps.detail: The operating volume is agreed with the aviation authority, marked and lit, and detect-and-avoid procedures are written before commercial operation.

prerequisites.why: the whole concept rests on a rope strong enough to hold a wing in a gale while staying light enough not to drag it down.
the wing must be stiff and strong yet light enough to fly and launch without a tower.
the wing is unstable and reacts in fractions of a second; controllers have flown hours-long flights but not years of unattended operation.
tethers, bearings and launch systems have not yet demonstrated multi-year service lives at sea or in remote sites.
most aviation authorities have no settled rules for a flying generator sharing airspace with aircraft.

pathway.milestone: small pilot systems in the tens to low hundreds of kilowatts; a US 600 kW prototype crashed in 2019 and its programme closed in 2020, and a Dutch developer ceased operations in 2022
pathway.unlocks: hard lessons on loads, control and the cost of reliability.

pathway.milestone: megawatt-class systems running autonomously for months, including through storms and launch/landing cycles
pathway.unlocks: the data needed to insure and finance a farm.

pathway.milestone: first commercial niche deployments on islands, remote industrial sites and small offshore arrays
pathway.unlocks: a market where diesel is the alternative and grid connection is expensive.

pathway.milestone: offshore farms of tethered wings on floating buoys or platforms
pathway.unlocks: access to strong, steady sea winds with a fraction of the steel and concrete of fixed turbines.
